items.evidence: After a page.reload() the test checks that statusInfo reads "Cancelled" and that fulfillButton has count 0 (diff lines 74-78). Both would fail if the cancel mutation never ran, because the order would reload as "Unfulfilled" with the fulfil button shown.
"Cancelled" after confirming (line 69), no fulfil action (line 70) and "Cancelled" after reload (line 77) are all asserted.

Extends the existing OrderPage and reuses its dialog, statusInfo and fulfillButton fields, plus findOrderId and ORDERS_SCENARIO. The new menu-button and menu-item locators were not in the suite before.
No waitForTimeout, sleeps or polling loops. It waits on the dialog becoming hidden.
Imports test from fixtures/test.ts, is not tagged parallel(), and does not write to the cache or the dumps.
Uses data-test-id locators. show-more-button is scoped to page-header and submit is scoped to the dialog.
Uses the orders scenario's existing unpaid order through findOrderId and sets nothing up in the spec.
No hard-coded ids. The order is looked up by its e2e metadata, and the status text is fixed UI copy, not a populatedb value.
Uses the default admin actor, which fits a ticket that does not name a permission. No UI sign-in and no credentials in the spec.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0. The spec is at e2e/tests/orders/order-cancel.spec.ts.
The new locators and the cancel() flow are on OrderPage. The spec only calls page-object methods and asserts on page-object locators.
The new members are readonly fields initialised from this.page, and the existing constructor is kept.
Has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (lines 54 and 59).
One test with a test.step for each stage.
The title "Cancel an unpaid, unfulfilled order #e2e" describes the behaviour and carries the tag.
The header comment at lines 43-48 says what the spec covers, why, and what it leaves out.
Every assertion is web-first.
Uses ORDERS_SCENARIO and the "unpaid" key. The only literals are status labels, as the suite itself does with "Draft". No money is compared.
No cleanup code and no unique-name tricks.
No timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
All relative imports keep the .ts extension, and nothing is imported from @playwright/test in the spec.
No any, no casts and no gql calls.
The comments give reasons (locator scoping, the portal, the vacuous-pass precondition, the order of assertions after reload) rather than narrating the next line.

structured_output.summary: Submission 4b11fbde meets all 23 checklist items. It adds a cancel() method and two scoped locators to the existing OrderPage, and one spec built on the orders scenario's unpaid order. The spec first checks that the order can be fulfilled, so the later "fulfil button gone" checks cannot pass by default. It then asserts the "Cancelled" status and the missing fulfil button, both before and after a reload, which shows the cancellation was saved on the server. The type check passes. Two small points don't count against any item: the planning file specs/order-cancel.md sits outside e2e/, and the dialog-hidden assertion repeats the wait already inside cancel().
